summary: Walter Clawiter specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt (c. 1950–1958) and held a post there from around 1958 to 1970.

Walter Couvreur worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and at Göttingen under Emil Sieg, later serving as Professor of Indo-European Linguistics at Ghent University from 1949.
Walter Denecke was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg by 1923. He studied under Hermann Jacobi and Walther Schubring.

Walter Elliot worked in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College and the College of Fort St. George, later serving in the Madras Government and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Madras (1859–1860).

Walter Emile van Wijk was an Indologist and historian who earned a doctorate in chemistry at Leiden University. He served as Privatdozent at Leiden, Director of Museon (1933–1938), and Director at the Cité Internationale Universitaire de Paris (1938–1953).

Walter Eugene Clark was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard, Berlin, and Bonn under Richard Pischel and Hermann Jacobi, he taught at the University of Chicago before becoming Wales Professor of Sanskrit at Harvard (1927–1950).
Walter Ewer worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Fort William College (c. 1803–1805) and served in the Bengal Civil Service from 1803 to 1840.

Walter Friedländer specialized in art history and Indology, earning his Ph.D. under Albrecht Weber at Berlin. He taught at the University of Freiburg, directed the Art Institute of Chicago, and served as Professor of Art History at New York University (1935–1966).

Walter Kaufmann worked in Indology and ethnomusicology, studying under Franz Schreker, Curt Sachs, Gustav Becking, and Paul Nettl. He led All India Radio's classical music department (c. 1937–1946) and was Professor of Ethnomusicology at Indiana University Bloomington (1957–1977).

Walter Liebenthal specialized in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. After earning his Dr. phil at Breslau, he held posts at the Harvard-Yenching Institute, Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, and served as honorary professor of Chinese Buddhism at the University of Tübingen (1964–1982).

Walter M. Spink was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University (Ph.D. c. 1949–1954). After teaching at Brandeis University, he served as a professor at the University of Michigan from around 1961 to 2000.

Walter Neisser worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and August Fick.

Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto from 1950 to 1965, held a post at Kyoto Women's University, and founded Moonspring Hermitage.

Walter Petersen was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who earned his Ph.D. from Yale University in 1908. He held posts at Bethany College, the University of Florida, and the University of Chicago, where he became Associate Professor of Comparative Philology in 1930.

Walter Porzig was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Jena, and Munich under Ernst Windisch, Ferdinand Sommer, and Wilhelm Streitberg. He held professorships at the Universities of Bern, Jena, Strasbourg, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz.

Walter Ruben specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying under Sten Konow, Hermann Jacobi, and Heinrich Lüders. He served as professor at Ankara University, the University of Chile, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he directed the Institut für Indienkunde (1950–1965).

Walter Simon was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, where he also taught, before serving as Reader and Professor of Chinese at SOAS, University of London, from 1936 to 1960.

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library and later served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2019.
Walter Sutton Page was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Reader of Bengali at the University of Oxford and at SOAS University of London from around 1920 to 1938.

Walter William Skeat was a linguist who was educated at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from around 1878 until 1912.
